title: Raising the House
hookLine: Ibrahim and Isma'il raise the foundations of the House, praying, accept this from us

lines: THE VALLEY HAS A SPRING NOW.
cards: If you've ever built something with your father, or your kid, you know it's never really about the shelf. One holds the board, one drives the screw, someone drops the level, somebody laughs.
The thing gets built, and something else gets built too. Back to the empty valley. There's a spring there now, and people have come to live around it.
Ibrahim comes back, and Isma'il is a grown man, sharpening arrows by the water. Ibrahim says, Allah has commanded me to build a House here. Will you help me?

teach.h: A CUBE OF STONE — AND THE QIBLA.
teach.b: The Ka'ba is a plain, cube-shaped stone building in the center of the great mosque in Mecca, draped in black cloth. The Qur'an tells believers, wherever they are, to turn their faces toward it in prayer.
That direction is called the qibla. A Muslim in Chicago or Jakarta faces this way on a prayer rug. Surah al-Baqarah gives us the building site.

teach.h: OUR LORD, ACCEPT THIS FROM US.
teach.b: Ibrahim and Isma'il are raising the foundations of the House, and as they work, they pray: our Lord, accept this from us. You are the Hearer, the Knower.
Not look what we built, not remember our names: they ask only that the work be received.
In the hadith in Bukhari, Isma'il carries the stones and Ibrahim sets them, and when the wall grows too high, Ibrahim stands on a stone to keep building.
That stone is still there, near the Ka'ba, called the Station of Ibrahim, and the Qur'an says to take the place where Ibrahim stood as a place of prayer.

teach.h: THE WEEK MEETS IN ONE PLACE.
teach.b: Some traditions say the House was first founded long before Ibrahim, even by Adam, and that Ibrahim raised it again. The Qur'an says he raised its foundations.
And this week's stories meet here: the valley where Hajar asked her question, the spring where she ran, the son who said do what you are commanded.
Ibrahim started these eleven days looking at a star, a moon, a sun, and loving what doesn't set. He ends them facing one House.

how: Muslims face the Ka'ba in Mecca for each of the five daily prayers, a direction called the qibla; pilgrims on Hajj and Umrah walk around it seven times and pray near the Station of Ibrahim.

games.q: you've just built the walls of a House for God with your father. as you set the stones, what do you pray?

our Lord, let people remember us.

games.why: our Lord, accept this from us; You are the Hearer, the Knower. they ask for nothing but that the work be received.

practice: Build something small your hands can finish in a minute, stack three books, fold a napkin, line up the pens on your desk, make your bed properly, and go slowly, putting the whole of yourself into one small job.
If you pray, you can say, as they did, our Lord, accept this from us. If not, notice what it feels like to make something without needing anyone to see it.

wordCard.voice: Ka'ba. The cube-shaped House in Mecca that Ibrahim and Isma'il raised, and that Muslims face in every prayer.

orig.note: Arabic: the Ka'ba, the cube-shaped House in Mecca.

carryVoice: Your line: accept it from us. Eleven days with Ibrahim: the stars, the idols, the fire, the guests, the valley, the spring, the dream, the House. Six weeks in.
